task: Summarize ambiguity rejection and selected pose/yaw derivation in 4 concise bullets.

local.response:
• **Ambiguity Rejection**: When multiple pose candidates are within the maximum distance threshold, the system groups segments by yaw angle similarity (within π/2) and selects the closest segment per group as a representative. If more than one representative exists, the result is marked as ambiguous.

• **Pose Selection**: Representatives are chosen based on minimum distance from the best pose, with ties broken by segment ID. The system prioritizes candidates that are both close in position and aligned in yaw direction to the best pose.

• **Yaw Derivation**: Yaw angles are compared using `_angle_difference()` to determine if segments are within π/2 of each other. This angle-based grouping ensures only similarly oriented segments are considered part of the same route branch.

• **Final Result**: If no competing candidates exist (i.e., only one valid pose), the result is accepted as "MATCHED". Otherwise, it's rejected as "AMBIGUOUS_ROUTE" due to conflicting route directions or positions.
